title: Roasted Cherry Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Oven-roasted cherries folded through a lighter custard.
summary: Our classic custard, made a little lighter and streaked with sweet cherries roasted until soft and syrupy. Deep red, jammy and summery.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast the cherries
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Toss the cherries with 70 g sugar in the tin and roast for 25 min, stirring once, until soft and sitting in syrup. Stir in the lemon juice, mash roughly and chill; roasting intensifies the fruit and cooks off water.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Warm the cream, milk and salt until steaming. Whisk the yolks with 80 g sugar, whisk in two ladles of hot dairy and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Over low heat, keep the custard moving until it thickens and reaches 77-80 °C. Do not let it simmer.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Pour through the sieve, stir in the vanilla and cool the bowl in iced water before refrigerating for a minimum of 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and ripple
steps.text: Churn until thick, then fold in the cold cherries and their syrup in streaks rather than mixing fully.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h, and enjoy within a week.

tips: Frozen stoned cherries work well; roast them a few minutes longer.
A common mistake is folding in warm cherries, which melts the ice cream. Chill them thoroughly.
Wear an apron when stoning cherries; the juice stains.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 1 week.
